subject: Errors with date x axis using geom_rect

messages.author: 439a20c9d67ff394
messages.subject: Errors with date x axis using geom_rect
parts:
Sigh. As usual, I'm sure I'm doing something stunningly dumb here, but
this simple example is giving me errors and for the life of me I can't
see why:

dat <-
data.frame(date=seq.Date(as.Date('2003-01-01'),as.Date('2005-01-01'),length.out=20),y=runif(20))
blocks <- data.frame(lev=c('a','b'),ymn=c(min(dat$y),0),ymx=c(0,max(dat
$y)),xmn=min(dat$date),xmx=max(dat$date))
ggplot(data=dat,aes(x=as.Date(date),y=y)) +
geom_rect(data=blocks,aes(xmin=as.Date(xmn),xmax=as.Date(xmx),ymin=ymn,ymax=ymx,fill=lev))

Specifically,

Error in as.Date.default(date) :
do not know how to convert 'date' to class "Date"

This plot works just fine:

ggplot(data=dat,aes(x=as.Date(date),y=y)) + geom_point()

I've tried various combinations of setting xmax and xmin inside aes()
and outside and I get the same error each time. Ideas?

messages.subject: Re: Errors with date x axis using geom_rect
parts:
Hi:

I managed to get a plot by simplifying (and spacing!!) the code:

> head(dat)
        date          y
1 2003-01-01 0.33943264
2 2003-02-08 0.62611516
3 2003-03-18 0.19749459
4 2003-04-26 0.30980879
5 2003-06-03 0.04741416
6 2003-07-12 0.75691885
> str(dat)
'data.frame':   20 obs. of  2 variables:
 $ date:Class 'Date'  num [1:20] 12053 12091 12130 12168 12207 ...
 $ y   : num  0.3394 0.6261 0.1975 0.3098 0.0474 ...

> blocks
  lev        ymn       ymx        xmn        xmx
1   a 0.04741416 0.0000000 2003-01-01 2005-01-01
2   b 0.00000000 0.9932042 2003-01-01 2005-01-01
> sapply(blocks, class)
      lev       ymn       ymx       xmn       xmx
 "factor" "numeric" "numeric"    "Date"    "Date"

all of which shows us that date, xmn and xmx are already Date objects and don't have to be coerced.

This gets us to
> ggplot(data=dat, aes(x=date, y=y)) +
+    geom_rect(data=blocks, aes(xmin = xmn, xmax=xmx,
+                               ymin=ymn, ymax=ymx, fill=lev))
Error in eval(expr, envir, enclos) : object 'y' not found

geom_rect() doesn't have a y argument, but you used y as an aesthetic in the base plot. This is a common gotcha - only define aesthetics in the base plot that will be present in all geoms. Removing y from the base plot aesthetic list renders a plot:

ggplot(data=dat, aes(x=date)) +
    geom_rect(data=blocks, aes(xmin = xmn, xmax=xmx,
                               ymin=ymn, ymax=ymx, fill=lev))

When you look at the two sets of x extremes in the blocks data frame, you can see they're the same, so the second overwrites the first. You can also see that your ymn at level a is higher than the max, so you still have a problem.

Let's add a lev factor to the original data frame for the purposes of illustration and use the ddply() function from plyr to get summaries:

dat2 <- dat
dat2$lev <- rep(c('a', 'b'), each = 10)
blocks <- ddply(dat2, 'lev', summarise, ymn = min(0, min(y)), ymx = max(0, max(y)),
                         xmn = min(date), xmx = max(date))
> blocks
  lev ymn       ymx        xmn        xmx
1   a   0 0.9734301 2003-01-01 2003-12-13
2   b   0 0.9932042 2004-01-20 2005-01-01

ggplot(data=dat2, aes(x=date)) +
   geom_rect(data=blocks, aes(xmin = xmn, xmax=xmx,
                              ymin=ymn, ymax=ymx, fill=lev), alpha = 0.3)

Hmm, probably not quite what you wanted. For this type of color split, it's better to let the y-ranges be infinite (or at least the same), and use the mean date (which just happens to be New Year's Day 2004 in this example, fortunately) to separate the x-ranges of the rectangles. Notice I'm also using alpha transparency to mute the background color. It would also make sense to plot a time series, so that's included below.

Reading between the lines, perhaps you were aiming for something like this. Notice that I'm defining the rectangle boundaries rather than summarizing them, as it provides more control.

blocks2 <- data.frame(lev = c('a', 'b'), ymn = -Inf, ymx = Inf,
                      xmn = c(min(dat2$date), mean(dat2$date)),
                      xmx = c(mean(dat2$date), max(dat2$date)))

# Notice how xmx for level a aligns with xmn for level b
> blocks2
  lev  ymn ymx        xmn        xmx
1   a -Inf Inf 2003-01-01 2004-01-01
2   b -Inf Inf 2004-01-01 2005-01-01

# Plot with a time series (we might as well use y since we went to
# the trouble of defining it :)
ggplot(data=dat2, aes(x=date)) + labs(fill = 'Level', linetype = 'Level') +
   geom_line(aes(y = y, linetype = lev), size = 1) +
   geom_rect(data=blocks2, aes(xmin = xmn, xmax=xmx,
                              ymin=ymn, ymax=ymx, fill=lev), alpha = 0.3)

You had the right idea by using a separate data frame to provide the appropriate inputs to geom_rect(), but the errors in this case are instructive and hopefully you have learned a couple of useful tricks. (For example, why did assigning Level to be the legend title for both fill and linetype work? What happens if you remove one?)

Cheers,
Dennis

messages.author: 439a20c9d67ff394
messages.subject: Re: Errors with date x axis using geom_rect
parts:
Gah! Thanks so much. The odd y ranges were just a typo on my part
(should've been runif(20,-1,1)); the intention was to have two
horizontally oriented rectangles each covering a vertical half the
plotting region, but ranging across the entire time series (x axis).

Dropping the extraneous coercions and removing the y aesthetic seem to
be the parts I was missing. I can even pinpoint the old habit from R's
base graphics of plotting some dummy data with type="n" and then
adding to it with points(), etc., which is why I had the y aesthetic
in there I think.

But the Inf/-Inf for the y endpoints is a neat trick, thanks!
